title: Multiple Polls Find Most Americans Think AI is Moving Too Fast
source_used: Tech Policy Press (poll roundup and visualization, full text read)
key_facts: In five national polls in 2026, the share of American adults saying AI is moving too fast, or should slow down, ranged from 55% to 77% (Tech Policy Press).

Each poll worded its question differently; the polls ran 23-26 Jan (1,005 registered voters), 16-18 Sep (2,051 adults), 24-27 Sep (1,202 adults), 24-28 Sep (2,140 adults) and 2-5 Oct 2026 (1,381 registered voters, margin of error +/-3.4 points).
Where results were broken out by party, Democrats were more concerned than Republicans, but in three of the four polls that asked by party, a majority of Republicans also said AI was moving too fast.

Quinnipiac: the share saying AI will do more harm than good in daily life was up 9 points since April 2025 (when it was 44%); it was 55% in March 2026 and the September result is little changed from March.
Pew (22-28 June 2026, 3,488 adults): the share more concerned than excited about AI in daily life was about the same as in June 2025, when it was 50%.

Context given by the article: after several incidents in recent months in which AI agents run by OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta intruded on third-party systems, industry leaders including Anthropic's Dario Amodei called for moderating the pace of AI, but the Trump administration rejected calls for a slowdown.
President Trump told reporters last month: 'whoever wins AI, wins'.
The Washington Post reported that Democrats have 'seized on' the administration's resistance to AI regulation as a line of attack in the midterm elections.
quote_evidence: In five national polls in 2026, the share of American adults saying AI is moving too fast or should slow down ranged from 55% to 77%.

In the polls that broke out results by party, Democrats were more concerned about AI than Republicans. But in three of the four polls that asked by party, a majority of Republicans also said AI was moving too fast.
The questions are worded differently, so compare the polls by their wording, not as a trend.
why_it_matters_hint: A broad majority of Americans across party lines want AI to move more slowly while the administration rejects a slowdown.
event_date: Roundup published 13 Oct 2026; polls January to 5 Oct 2026
notes: A roundup and chart page whose per-poll results sat in graphics that were not captured as text, so the 55% and 77% ends of the range cannot be tied to named polls. The article says its details were checked against sources and that it was built with an AI tool. The pollsters are named only in part (AP-NORC, Quinnipiac and Pew appear in the text).
